thread:
eli: Heads-up — flash-attn upstream merged a kernel rename/selector change and I'm seeing a ~15-25% perf regression on T4 nightly for seq_len=2048. Repro steps and traces below. Anyone else hit this?

maria: PR: https://github.com/flash-attention/flash-attention/pull/642 — commit abcdef1 renamed several kernels and changed the fallback ordering :eyes:

sam: Is this the paged-attn work or the fused kernel tweak? We have both patches in flight so need to separate causes.

eli: It's the selector logic, not paged per se — our runtime tries to pick `flash_attn_v2` but upstream now exposes `flash_attn_gemm` for certain shapes so it falls back to a slower generic fused kernel. Quick profiler excerpt: 
```
# run: ./runtest --model gpt2 --seq 2048 --bs 4
tokens/sec before: 18.6k
tokens/sec after: 14.2k  <-- ~23% drop
hotspots: fused_gemm_kernel (40%), generic_attn (25%), cuda_memcpy (12%)
```

jamie: I can reproduce locally on a T4 VM. Command I ran: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32 ./bench_attention --flash --seq 2048` — same regression.

infra-bot: CI alert: nightly/dedicated/rt-perf failed (job 4421). Link: https://ci.internal/reports/4421 — perf regression detected vs baseline.

maria: Short-term mitigations: pin FA to commit before the rename OR add an alias map in our kernel selector that maps new kernel names to the ones we expect. I pushed a draft mapping PR: https://git.internal/r/inference/runtime/pulls/1987 — currently experimental.

sam: FYI vLLM merged a KV-cache layout change today that could interact with paged-attn. PR: https://github.com/vllm/vllm/pull/310 — it changes KV order (seq-major -> layer-major). We should run our paged-attn regression suite against that too.

jamie: Also saw xFormers patch that drops their fused kernel shim (https://github.com/facebookresearch/xformers/commit/ff12a3). If vendors stop shipping the prebuilt fused blobs we fall back to slower kernels during build. Filed vendor-ticket 203 to confirm.

eli: TL;DR of root causes we're tracking: kernel rename/selector change (flash-attn), KV-cache layout change (vLLM) and vendor build drops (xFormers / prebuilt fused kernels). All three can produce similar perf symptoms so need to triage carefully. :thinking_face: 

maria: Proposed immediate action items:
- revert/pin FA in our nightly until mapping lands
- add unit that verifies kernel name list at startup (fail-build if missing)
- run vLLM KV-layout integration tests on paged-attn CI matrix
- open an upstream issue in FA describing the perf regression + our suggested alias approach (assign to @maintainers)

sam: I'll own the vLLM integration runs and add tests to catch KV-order mismatches.
jamie: I'll validate vendor build artifacts and follow up on ticket 203.
eli: I'll land the runtime alias map patch behind a flag and gate it to experimental until we verify.

maria: @eli can you add a tiny repro script (2-3 lines) to the PR description so upstream can reproduce quickly? That speeds triage.
eli: Yep — will add a minimal repro + perf numbers.

infra-bot: Note: regression alert created: PERF-1771001234. Follow-up thread: #perf-investigations.

sam: One more note — paged-attn tests show KV cache evictions spike when we run with batch sizes >8. Might be separate but worth watching.

eli: Good call. For now everyone: add any new observations to the PR comments and to the perf issue so we don't lose traces. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
